what_happened: The the person running Athena's nmnv request said when a dependency counts as met. It did not say what counts as a dependency. The planner treats any job id that appears in a request's text as a dependency. Several requests cited failed jobs only as evidence, and that included the the person running Athena's own urgent fixes. The planner read those citations as dependencies on jobs that never succeeded, so the requests were held forever. The the person running Athena logged a mistake and queued a fix.
cause: Dependency detection is a loose text heuristic with no defined meaning of "dependency". A job id in prose is treated the same as a declared prerequisite. Nothing replays the inference over real past requests to see how often an id is only a citation. Nothing flags a request held by a job that has failed or been rejected. The first sign was urgent work stuck in the queue.
prevention: Make dependencies explicit and narrow. The planner should count only ids in a dedicated dependency line (for example "Depends on: <id>"), not ids anywhere in the text. Add a check that replays the inference over all past queued requests, and fails if any request that cites ids gains a dependency it did not declare. Also warn when a request is held by a job that is failed, rejected or abandoned, instead of holding it silently.
proposed_request:
Change the planner so a queued request has a dependency on another job only when the request declares it on a line starting "Depends on:" followed by job ids. A job id mentioned anywhere else in the text (evidence, history, a cited failed job) must never create a dependency. Acceptance:
- A request that cites a failed job id in its body, with no "Depends on:" line, is planned as having no dependencies and is not held.
- A request with "Depends on: <id>" is held until that job has landed.
- A request held by a job that is failed, rejected or abandoned is reported by the plan with the job id and the reason, not held silently.
- A test replays the planner over every past queued request and shows that no request gets a dependency it did not declare with a "Depends on:" line.
- The request format documentation states the "Depends on:" rule.
